column.name: longitude
column.comment: Current longitude of the mobile unit: ex 123.12345 Degree

column.name: acc
column.comment: ACC -- The engine start/stop staus.It's on when you turn the ignition switch. But deos not mean engine is running. To determine engine start/stop status, this has to be combined with batt voltage.

column.name: in1
column.comment: Input port1 status. In1, In2 , in3 and in4 can be configured to monitor status of any device for on or off. Ex: doors, tail gate etc

column.name: out1
column.comment: With out1 & out2 ports, 2 devices can be control through GPRS/SMS commands from application. ex: turn off the fuel pump to stop the car

column.name: out2
column.comment: With out1 & out2 ports, 2 devices can be control through GPRS/SMS commands from application. ex: turn off the fuel pump to stop the car

column.name: eventcode
column.comment: Event Code 0 None 1 ACC status is ON 2 ACC status is OFF 3 Input port status changed 4 Emergency 5 Main power disconnect 6 Case open 7 Over speed 8 Server command execute success (GPRS or SMS) 9 Server command execute failure (GPRS or SMS) 10 Distance exceed 11 Geo-fence detected

column.name: adc1
column.comment: Analog input from unit in Voltage like a normal volt meter. Value 0 - 30V (123 -> 12.3 Vol) Ex: It can be connected to fuel level sensor to read the level of the fuel. Value is in Volt. So it needs to be converted to graph with some calibration. Because each car have different shape and caracteristic of the voltage differentiation. Also it can be connected to measure the temperature of refrigerated trucks.

column.name: batt
column.comment: BATTERY VOLT. Car battery (unit power input) voltage value, Divide by 10, 144->14.4 Volt For normal car, engine off voltage is around 12.5. Engine on is more than 13.8 V. Please note this value is different for different types of vehicles
